originality.rationale: The exact stationary variance mixture and the ordinary rapid-switching Gaussian regime are explicitly prior results. The final claim instead gives the nested q→∞ crossover scales x∼q^{1/4} and x∼√q, globally unique selected variance, sharp prefactor, posterior weak-state selection and inversion from rate curvature/tail. The primary 2023 main article analyzes a different large-population extreme-value regime. Search results for related collective rare-energy and boundary-layer work have different asymptotic control parameters. Implicit coverage in supplements or a broader unpublished asymptotic derivation remains a residual risk. Two directly related published switching-gas findings were materially compared: one proves large-N empirical-energy tails, the other large-N extreme-value edge selection; neither uses the single-particle, rate-q scaling or weak-phase posterior.
residual_risks: An exact 2023 finite-q stationary Gaussian mixture is mathematically stronger as a complete distributional description; novelty relies on the two distinct singular scales, explicit sharp prefactor and selected hidden state.

value.rationale: The rapidly switching trap has a Gaussian central law that fails exponentially at the physically natural displacement scale sqrt(q). The exact earlier quartic relative-density correction, later nonquadratic rate, prefactor and monotone conditional hidden-state recovery identify two sharp experimentally relevant regimes and allow individual stiffness recovery from rare positions, beyond mean effective stiffness. The global strict inequalities and two tail limits are structural, not a parameter-specific numerical exercise; no downstream theorem is needed.
